hooks.hook: You’ve had filter coffee. Now meet its 1970s ancestor in Koramangala.
Why do Bangaloreites start their day with this?
Filter coffee is how Bangalore wakes up.
This isn’t just coffee—it’s the city’s morning rhythm.

chosen_hook.hook: Filter coffee is how Bangalore wakes up.
chosen_hook.reason: It creates a vivid, relatable image of filter coffee as a daily ritual that encapsulates Bangalore’s culture in a way that feels authentic and specific to the audience.

beats.vo_line: Filter coffee is how Bangalore wakes up.
It’s the first thing you order at 7 a.m.
Steam rises from the V6 machine in every office.
You’ll find it in alleyways, beside temples, and at the end of your commute.
The ritual is simple: milk, sugar, and a cup that’s always full.
It’s more than a drink—it’s a ritual, a habit, a comfort.

storyboard.title: Why Bangalore Loves Filter Coffee
storyboard.hook: Filter coffee is how Bangalore wakes up.

shots.visual_prompt: A steaming V6 filter coffee machine in a small Bangalore office kitchen, early morning light streaming through a half-open window, milk froth on the surface, steam rising in slow motion.
shots.overlay_text: Filter coffee is how Bangalore wakes up.

shots.visual_prompt: A young professional in a crisp shirt, holding a white ceramic cup of filter coffee, walking past a glass office door, sunlight reflecting off the cup.
A close-up of a V6 machine in a tiny alleyway, steam curling up from the spout, a metal tray with a few cups beside it, old and new architecture in the background.
A shot of a temple gate with a small filter coffee stall beside it, a man in a traditional shawl pouring coffee into a cup, a few customers waiting, the sun setting behind the temple.

A close-up of a hand adding milk and sugar to a cup, the sugar dissolving in the dark coffee, steam rising, the cup held by a woman in a saree, background showing a bustling street with rickshaws and motorbikes.

A wide shot of a small, dimly lit filter coffee shop in the evening, a few customers sitting at low tables, the air filled with the sound of chatter and the clink of cups, the owner behind the counter.
A person sipping from a cup of filter coffee at a corner table, the table cluttered with a laptop, a phone, and a half-eaten biscuit, a fan humming softly in the background.
